name: Citation Management Conventions
description: This module defines the naming, formatting, and structural style conventions to follow whenever writing, implementing, or reviewing citation management code or output, so results stay consistent with the existing citation management style guide.
content:
This module defines the naming, formatting, and structural style conventions to follow whenever writing, implementing, or reviewing citation management code or output, so results stay consistent with the existing citation management style guide.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Document any non-obvious citation management decision with a short rationale so future readers understand the 'why', not just the 'what'.
2. Prefer explicit, readable citation management solutions over clever ones that are hard to verify.
3. Keep citation management outputs reproducible: fix seeds, record versions, and avoid hidden non-determinism where it matters.
4. When citation management decisions are ambiguous, favor the option that is easiest to reverse or extend later.
5. Keep citation management changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.
6. State assumptions about citation management explicitly before proceeding, rather than leaving them implicit.
7. Check that citation management terminology is used consistently throughout, matching existing conventions in the surrounding context.
8. When multiple citation management strategies are viable, name the trade-off explicitly rather than silently picking one.
9. Re-check edge cases relevant to citation management (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.
10. Surface known limitations of a chosen citation management approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.
11. Measure before optimizing any citation management bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.
12. Prefer the simplest citation management approach that satisfies the requirement over a more general one that isn't needed yet.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Avoid mixing unrelated citation management concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.
- Do not apply generic citation management advice without checking it fits the specific context at hand.
- Avoid introducing new citation management abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.

CLOSING NOTE
Revisit these citation management guidelines if the task's constraints change significantly during the work.
